courses.title: Introduction to Engineering
courses.description: This course is an introduction to engineering design through a variety of team projects, including experimentation, data analysis, and the development of computer skills. Students will be exposed to several engineering disciplines through project design and problem solving for the purpose of providing information to assist them in choosing a major.
courses.advisories: ESL D272. and ESL D273., or ESL D472. and ESL D473., or eligibility for ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005. Pre-algebra or equivalent (or higher), or appropriate placement beyond pre-algebra

metadata.Transferability: Transferable to both UC and CSU

metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Analyze, graph and develop a formula for a given data set. Prepare and write technical specifications and documentation, and be able to orally present them. Work collaboratively on an engineering team.

courses.title: Programming and Problem-Solving in MATLAB
courses.description: This course utilizes the MATLAB environment to provide students with a working knowledge of computer-based problem-solving methods relevant to science and engineering. It introduces the fundamentals of procedural and object-oriented programming, numerical analysis, and data structures. Examples and assignments in the course are drawn from practical applications in engineering, physics, and mathematics.

courses.title: Statics
courses.description: This course covers the principles of statics as applied to particles and rigid bodies in two and three dimensions; vector solutions for concentrated and distributed loads; the determination of centroids and moments of inertia and the effects of dry friction; and programming computer solutions.
courses.prerequisites: ENGR D010., MATH D001B or MATH D01BH and PHYS D004A

metadata.Transferability: Transferable to both UC and CSU
metadata.Prerequisite(s): ENGR D010., MATH D001B or MATH D01BH and PHYS D004A
metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Analyze two- and three-dimensional force systems on rigid bodies in static equilibrium using vector and scalar analysis methods.

courses.title: Introduction to Circuit Analysis
courses.description: This course introduces the analysis of linear circuits; first- and second-order differential equations describing RLC circuits; the natural and forced response of simple circuits; the development of steady-state sinusoidal circuit analysis for the network differential equations; and the study of Thevenin, Norton, and operational amplifiers.
courses.prerequisites: MATH D001D or MATH D01DH; and PHYS D004B (may be taken concurrently)

metadata.Transferability: Transferable to both UC and CSU
metadata.Prerequisite(s): MATH D001D or MATH D01DH; and PHYS D004B (may be taken concurrently)
metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Analyze circuits containing resistive, capacitive, inductive passive elements, along with op-amps interconnected to voltage and current sources. Use circuit laws and network theorems to solve DC steady state circuits, RC, RL, and RLC DC circuit transients and sinusoidal AC steady state circuits.
metadata.Course Description: This course introduces the analysis of linear circuits; first- and second-order differential equations describing RLC circuits; the natural and forced response of simple circuits; the development of steady-state sinusoidal circuit analysis for the network differential equations; and the study of Thevenin, Norton, and operational amplifiers.

courses.title: Introduction to Circuit Analysis Laboratory
courses.description: This course offers practical verification of theorems and concepts learned through experimentation. It will include experiments in DC and AC circuits involving the utilization of a variety of instruments, such as DC/AC meters, regulated power supplies, signal generators, and oscilloscopes.

metadata.Transferability: Transferable to both UC and CSU
metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Use circuit simulator to verify circuit performance. Use DC/AC equipment to measure DC/AC signals in various circuit configuration.

courses.title: Properties of Materials
courses.description: This course is an introduction to engineering materials, including pure metals, binary alloys, steels, semiconductors, plastics, and polymers, with an introduction to the mechanics of materials, including basic material failure mechanisms.
courses.prerequisites: CHEM D001B (or CHEM D01BH), MATH D001C (or MATH D01CH), and PHYS D004A

metadata.Transferability: Transferable to both UC and CSU
metadata.Prerequisite(s): CHEM D001B (or CHEM D01BH), MATH D001C (or MATH D01CH), and PHYS D004A
metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Evaluate the appropriateness of material(s) to meet engineering design criteria based on the materials properties and performance.
metadata.Course Description: This course is an introduction to engineering materials, including pure metals, binary alloys, steels, semiconductors, plastics, and polymers, with an introduction to the mechanics of materials, including basic material failure mechanisms.
